messages:
sam_sales: Hey team — Acme Corp POC is failing. They POST a single embeddings request with ~3MB JSON and get a 413 from our gateway. They need a demo tomorrow. Any quick options?

alex_eng: Which endpoint exactly? embeddings or chat? Can you paste the error body/log?

kaitlyn_poc: embeddings.batch v1 — they send ~200 docs as one array (each doc has some base64 binary blobs). Sample error we saw: `HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large` from gateway.

maria_se: Pasting redacted curl + response: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @payload.json
HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
{"error":"request body exceeds configured limit"}
```

leo_infra: Our default gateway max_request_body_bytes is 2097152 (2MB). That explains the 413. Options: 1) bump gateway limit per-route/customer, 2) ask customer to chunk their payload server-side, 3) accept gzipped payloads. Quick notes: bumping is doable but needs security acknowledgement and a canary deploy.

sam_sales: Customer would prefer single request for UX. Are there docs on gzip support? Also if we ask them to chunk, will they be charged more? Need pricing answer for the sales thread.

maria_se: We bill embeddings per embedding unit (tokens/inputs). Chunking will likely create more units depending on overlap; rough estimate for their dataset: chunking into 4 requests ≈ ~1.1–1.4x cost. We can give exact calc if they share average doc sizes.

alex_eng: Implementation note: our embeddings endpoint accepts Content-Encoding: gzip and will transparently decompress. If the client gzips the JSON (gzip -> send) they can reduce size substantially. Example:
```
cat payload.json | gzip -c > payload.json.gz
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \
  --data-binary @payload.json.gz
```
This avoids chunking and shouldn't affect billing (we bill on decoded content).

kaitlyn_poc: Confirmed with Acme — they can gzip on their side for the demo. Good immediate workaround.

leo_infra: For completeness: I can push a per-customer gateway config to increase body limit to 8MB for the trial window (48h). Security flagged it but said temporary increases are OK with WAF tuning. ETA: 4–6 hours to canary and 6–8 for full roll.

security_bot: Flag: increasing gateway body limit may expose WAF bypass vectors for large payloads; recommend enabling size-based scanning and logging for the customer route.

sam_sales: Ok — plan: (A) ask Acme to gzip for demo (immediate), (B) leo to prepare temporary 8MB increase if gzip not feasible, (C) maria to send cost delta note for chunking option. I'll tell the customer those options.

alex_eng: I'll open a tiny client patch that detects >1.5MB payload and auto-gzips. PR link: https://github.com/redwood/client/pull/789 (WIP). Will tag @kaitlyn_poc for testing.

deploy-bot: Started gateway-config canary for route: customers/acme/policy — canary on 2 nodes. CI passed.

maria_se: Cost note to include in customer email: "If unable to gzip and you chunk into N requests, estimated cost multiplier ~1.2x–1.4x depending on overlap. We can provide exact numbers if you share average doc lengths."

sam_sales: Great, I'll update Acme and keep them in the loop. Thanks everyone :tada:

kaitlyn_poc: I'll run a quick end-to-end with gzipped payload and post results here in ~30m.

alex_eng: If gzipping fails for any reason, fallback is chunk+backoff. I can ship the client patch in next hour and we can attach it to the POC repo.

leo_infra: Noted. I'll start the temporary limit change but tag it with expiration 48h. Will coordinate with security.

sam_sales: Perfect — closing loop after E2E. Attaching ticket: POC-12345.
